reconcile.note: Gill limits Deuteronomy's intermarriage ban to the idolatrous Canaanite nations, excluding proselytes and foreign unions like Joseph's Egyptian marriage.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Will God destroy those that intermarry?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/intermarriage.html) (2013).

sides.snippet: To Joseph in the land of Egypt were born Manasseh and Ephraim, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, bore to him.
sides.verseText: To Joseph in the land of Egypt were born Manasseh and Ephraim, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, bore to him.

sides.snippet: so will the anger of Yahweh be kindled against you, and he will destroy you quickly.
sides.verseText: For he will turn away your son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of Yahweh be kindled against you, and he will destroy you quickly.
